thread:
deploy-bot: ALERT: Canary failures detected for service=redwood-inference-api env=prod-canary at 1760004321. rate of 5xx > 4% over 2m. Canary deployment id=canary-2026-03-15-17:02. tagging: release-20260315.

oncall-bot: Paging @jess (on-call). Incident created: INC-2026-0315-01.

jess: I’m on it. collecting logs from canary and comparing image digests. can someone confirm the artifact tag that CI pushed? @omar?

omar: I triggered the rollout earlier. CI reported success: image=redwood/inference-api:release-20260315 digest=sha256:abc123def456. I’ll pull digests from registry now.

sasha: seeing elevated 502s from canary pods, also unusual latency spikes. quick gists:
```
kubectl get pods -n prod-canary -o wide
NAME                                   READY STATUS   RESTARTS
inference-api-canary-5f8d6b7c9-ptq4   1/1   Running  0
inference-api-canary-5f8d6b7c9-xn2z   1/1   Running  0
```
logs show: repeated `invalid model manifest` errors from startup.

maria: digging into image digests: registry shows tag release-20260315 -> digest sha256:abc123def456, but KUBE cluster shows pod image digest sha256:deadbeef9999 for the running container. that is a mismatch.

jess: whoa. tag points to abc123..., but infra runtime pulled deadbeef... Could be registry cache or proxy returning a different layer/digest for the same tag. Any chance the image registry got a force-push?

omar: CI artifact storage shows first build (build#1201) produced sha256:deadbeef9999 but was later rebuilt (build#1202) with same tag release-20260315 and digest sha256:abc123def456. CI should have failed on tag collision — it didn't. Looks like our CI allows tag reuse if a new build succeeds.

sasha: that explains why canary got an older build. older build has incompatible schema changes -> `invalid model manifest`. customer-facing errors match.

jess: immediate mitigation: 1) flip kill-switch feature-flag to route traffic away from canary path and 2) stop further rollouts and pause CI tagging. Maria, can you flip the flag? @maria

maria: flipping feature flag `canary-serving-enabled=false` for prod now. -> :white_check_mark: traffic diverted.

oncall-bot: Incident state: mitigation in progress.Assigned to jess, omar.

jess: next: perform a rollback of canary to the known-good digest sha256:feedface0001 (release-20260308). omar, can you apply the pin manifest?

omar: applying pinned image manifest to prod-canary now:
```
kubectl set image deploy/inference-api-canary inference-api=redwood/inference-api@sha256:feedface0001 -n prod-canary
```
Rollout started. Watching pods.

sasha: pods coming up with feedface digest, healthchecks passing. 5xx down to 0.6% within 3m.

jess: good. hold on exposure — do not promote tag until artifact pipeline fixes.

maria: CI team: we need an emergency change: prevent reuse of tags in registry or enforce immutable tags by digest. Also add a tag-collision alert to CI.

omar: noted. I’ll open CI PR to fail on tag already exists unless `--force` flag used with explicit approval. Also add a pipeline step to record digest to artifact metadata store.

kevin: heads-up: possibility of registry cache poisoning. our edge cache (proxy.gcr-cache) had recent errors 2h ago. checking logs now.

maria: I see proxy.gcr-cache had a cache eviction/repopulate at 15:10 UTC. It returned older layer for `release-20260315` briefly due to eventual consistency window. Repository allowed tag overwrite, so older digest reappeared under same tag.

jess: root cause summary (working): CI allowed tag reuse; registry/proxy eventual consistency returned older digest for same tag during propagate; canary pulled older incompatible build -> failures.

jess: customer impact: only canary got affected; feature flag prevented broad blast. No customer-facing incidents recorded beyond canary monitoring thresholds. We should still notify any downstream teams that rely on canary metrics.

oncall-bot: Incident timeline note saved.

omar: I'll revert the registry tag policy to immutable and re-run a rebuild with new unique tag. Releasing fixed artifact as `release-20260315v2` and will update manifests after QA.

sasha: post-mortem action items: 
- CI: prevent tag reuse / add digest pinning in pipeline (owner: omar)
- Registry: enforce immutable tags / fix cache eviction consistency (owner: kevin)
- Deploy: add image digest check before rollout (owner: jess)
- SRE: add an alert for image digest mismatch between registry and node (owner: sasha)
- Docs: update runbook for canary kill-switch and tagging policy (owner: maria)

jess: I'll keep INC open until CI fix merged and one stable deploy completed. Good job team.

maria: INC-2026-0315-01 status -> mitigated. Will update customers if needed.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-01 updated: mitigated -> monitoring.

jess: closing notes: add an automated pre-deploy verification step that compares registry digest for a tag vs the digest pulled by kubelet on the first pod. If mismatch, abort rollout. I'll file the ticket.

kevin: filing infra bug for proxy.gcr-cache eventual consistency and proposing TTL change.

omar: CI PR: https://git.internal.redwood/ci/pipelines/pull/1123 (WIP) — will link once ready.

sasha: thanks everyone.

deploy-bot: RESOLVE: Canary alert resolved at 1760005199.
